title: Arrival contingency windows & SKU fallbacks
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures recommended contingency windows for GPU arrivals and an operational SKU-fallback hierarchy for t = lead_time disruptions (carrier delays, customs, supply shock). The goal is to give SRE/Procurement/Capacity planners a concise set of heuristics and runbook actions that can be automated or executed manually during high-friction windows.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to committed fleet orders (reserved and spot leases not covered here).
- Focus regions: us-west, us-east, eu-west, apac-southeast.
- SKUs grouped by performance tier and footprint: P-tier (highest perf), M-tier (mainline), E-tier (economy/quantized), R-tier (refurbished).
- Lead-time delta = actual ETA - expected ETA. Contingency windows are triggered when delta > threshold.
- This is complementary to the existing reorder/runway sheets; it is oriented to handling late arrivals rather than initial SKU mix planning.

1) Contingency window definitions (operational):
- Green window (on-time): delta <= 7 days. Monitor only; no automatic actions besides standard acceptance.
- Amber window (early stress): 8 <= delta <= 21 days. Trigger: inventory attention, short-term borrowing options, accelerate alternative shipments if low runway < 28 days.
- Red window (critical): delta > 21 days. Trigger: execute SKU-fallback, region-to-region reshuffle, engage executive procurement, consider short-term leasing.

2) Trigger inputs (automated signals):
- Shipping provider status update (delays flagged)
- Customs hold >= 72 hours in manifest feed
- Vendor-provided revised ETA (official)
- Transit sensor loss > 48 hours
- Capacity burn rate > forecast + 15% for that region (7-day rolling)

3) SKU-fallback hierarchy (preferred ordering when primary SKU delayed):
- Primary SKU -> Mapped fallback sequence (pre-approved by finance):
  - Example: A100-80GB (P-tier) fallback list = [A100-40GB (M-tier), H100-80GB (M-tier), A30-40GB (E-tier)]
  - Fallback rules: prefer same-generation architectures where latency-sensitive features depend on fw compatibility. If incompatible, prefer higher-latency but available SKU and put requests through quantization/compilation profile adjustments.
- Refurb/refleet as last resort: R-tier only if shortfall would break SLOs for >1 high-priority customers.

4) Regional reshuffle cadence (when to move inventory between regions):
- Heuristic: if region shortfall forecast > 10% of committed capacity for next 14 days, evaluate reshuffle.
- Prefer intra-continent moves first (e.g., eu-west <-> eu-central).
- Shipping cost vs SLA impact: construct quick net-cost delta = (estimated expedited shipping + customs fees) - (penalty/SLA cost avoided). If net-cost delta < threshold (finance-configured), proceed.
- Minimum transfer batch = 4 GPUs for rack-level efficiency; smaller transfers need exec approval.

5) Actions by contingency level (runbook):
- Amber:
  - 1) Notify capacity owners and list affected services/routes.
  - 2) Increase autoscaling buffer on key routes (+10%).
  - 3) Evaluate short-term spot lease vendors (target <= 30 days).
  - 4) Place conditional order for fallback SKUs (non-binding hold) for up to 2 weeks pending ETA updates.
- Red:
  - 1) Immediately escalate to Procurement lead and SRE on-call.
  - 2) Initiate SKU-fallback: switch canary traffic to available SKU variant with quant/profile changes, run smoke-eval on sample prompts within 2 hours.
  - 3) Rearrange scheduled canaries/cutovers to reduce risk while fallback active.
  - 4) If reshuffle chosen, kick off expedited transfer and update inventory ledger.
  - 5) If >30% committed capacity at risk in a region, prepare a leasing/market-purchase worksheet and legal review for accelerated contracts.

6) Example contingency calculation (quick check):
- Input: expected ETA 2024-10-10; vendor revised ETA 2024-11-05 => delta = 26 days => Red.
- Current runway in eu-west = 22 days at current burn; threshold runway for action = 28 days.
- Decision: Red -> schedule 12 GPUs of fallback H100-80GB, task autoscale changes, open lease quote.

7) Compatibility/quality guardrails for fallbacks:
- For each fallback pairing, we maintain a compatibility tag: binary compat = yes/no (model weight format + attention kernel parity). If compat=no, require compilation pass + 10% latency increase allowed band.
- Maintain a small prompt-suite (50 prompts) per customer group to smoke-check quality after fallback. Threshold: >5% increase in hallucination triggers manual rollback.

8) Pre-authorized finance caps and approvals:
- Amber actions: procurement can place holds up to $75k without exec.
- Red actions: up to $250k can be auto-procured with CFO pre-approval for emergencies; anything above requires COO sign-off.

9) Data sources and instrumentation to feed automation:
- inbound: vendor-ETA webhook, carrier-status API, customs portal scrape, vendor-portal CSV feed
- internal: regional burn rate telemetry, per-model token burn, scheduled rollouts and reserve commitments
- outputs: automated slack alerts to #capacity-alerts, inventory delta table, procurement hold ticket (JIRA)

10) Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact compatibility matrix format and register all SKU pairs (Action: Marcus to own; due 2024-10-10).
- Build a one-click reshuffle flow in the ops console with cost estimator (Action: Hannah; PoC 2024-11-01).
- Clarify tax/customs expedited thresholds for APAC lanes (Action: Legal + Procurement; due 2024-10-20).

Appendix A — Short checklist for on-call SRE when Amber/Red triggers:
- Confirm delta and verify vendor update (screenshot + ticket).
- Post short note in incident channel with ETA, region, affected models and expected customer% impacted.
- If fallback content selected, run pre-registered smoke suite and upload results to the ticket.
- If reshuffle, mark expected arrival into destination DC and annotate rack allocation.

Appendix B — Quick mapping table (text):
- us-west: prefer A100 family -> fallback H100/A30 (if software-compatible); leasing partners: LeaseFast, GPUShare
- us-east: prefer H100 -> fallback A100-40GB / A30; leasing partners: RackBorrow, LeaseFast
- eu-west: prefer A100 -> fallback H100-80GB (regionally available) / refurbished pools
- apac-southeast: prefer A10/H100 mix -> fallback to locally-sourced refurbished + express-leases (higher customs risk)

End notes:
- Keep this living: update the fallback lists whenever we onboard a new SKU (procurement ticket must add compatibility tags).
- This doc intends to be operationally actionable and scriptable; next step is to convert triggers into the orchestration playbook (infra-ops repo).
